shape: python scripts/day-mode.py blind. The first ten were measured over the tree at 514f5ae; scripts/dev/build-ordinary-english.py was added on 2026-09-04 after b66b60f landed.
note: Shrink-only, same contract as config/tmp-leak-baseline.json. These are the source files that a test under tests/ mentions and that day mode can select NO SPECIFIC TEST for: neither the import route nor the string-literal route reaches them. Each was traced by hand to the site that reaches it; the reason below says which mechanism, so a reader can tell a real hole from a coincidental word match. Ten of the eleven are reached by a tree sweep that IS in the mandatory core and therefore does run on every day-mode invocation, which is why day mode is safe over them today; they are recorded here because the sweep is a tree-wide invariant check and not a test of the file's behaviour, and because a sweep's glob can be narrowed later without anything saying so. Adding an entry is a deliberate act and the wrong first move: when tests/test_day_mode_blind_spot.py goes red, look first at whether the literal route can be taught the shape the new test uses, because every shape it learns closes the hole for every future file at once.

reasons..claude/skills/playwright/scripts/pw.py: NO TEST EXERCISES IT AT ALL. The only mention under tests/ is a prose docstring in tests/test_two_skill_contracts_that_were_declared_and_never_measured.py, recording that a yt-pulse reference doc told a reader to run a bare `pw.py` that resolves nowhere. The other grep hits are the substring 'pw' inside password literals. This is an untested file, which is a coverage question and not day mode's to answer; it sits here only because the mention check cannot tell prose from a driver.

reasons.scripts/dev/build-ordinary-english.py: Arrived 2026-09-04 with the ordinary-English floor and is the eleventh entry. It is NOT swept by tests/test_import_purity.py, whose globs are 'scripts/*.py' and '.claude/skills/**/*.py' and stop one level above scripts/dev/. It IS read by three tree-wide sweeps that glob 'scripts/**/*.py' through tracked_paths: tests/test_a_deputy_admin_the_code_never_had.py, tests/test_a_guard_that_crashed_on_a_file_that_vanished_mid_walk.py and tests/test_a_quote_marker_that_ate_the_claim.py, all three verified present in the mandatory core on 2026-09-04, so they run on every day-mode invocation. Those sweeps check tree-wide invariants over its text, not its behaviour: nothing anywhere EXECUTES this generator, and its only mention by name under tests/ is a prose line in the docstring of test_the_artifact_is_the_one_committed_here, telling a reader how to regenerate config/ordinary-english.txt. That is a coverage question and not day mode's to answer. What makes the gap narrow rather than open is the digest: the artifact's SHA-256 is pinned in that same test, so a regeneration that changed the vocabulary fails the suite as a visible re-pin even though the generator itself is never run.
reasons.scripts/engine-audit.py: Imported and executed in a subprocess by tests/test_import_purity.py through the same tracked_paths glob, matching its 'scripts/*.py' half. The only other mention, in tests/test_a_rotation_that_could_forget_what_it_had_checked.py, is prose. In the mandatory core.
reasons.scripts/migrations/0001_baseline.py: THE ONE GENUINE HOLE OF THE TEN, and the shape worth reading. It is NOT swept by tests/test_import_purity.py, whose glob is 'scripts/*.py' and stops one level above scripts/migrations/. It is exercised by tests/test_five_reports_that_outran_their_evidence.py, which calls registered_migrations() from scripts/migrations/__init__.py; that function discovers the module with pkgutil.iter_modules and loads it with importlib.import_module(f'{__name__}.{name}'). The module name is assembled at run time from a discovered string, so neither an import edge nor a literal exists anywhere for day mode to find. A change to this file selects no test that runs it.
reasons.scripts/scrutinize-record.py: Imported and executed in a subprocess by tests/test_import_purity.py through the 'scripts/*.py' glob. Every other apparent reference points at the different module scripts/utils/scrutinize_record.py (underscore), and tests/test_scrutinize_record.py names the hyphenated CLI only in its docstring. In the mandatory core.
